quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You need a lab technician to set up equipment early. Subject: Early set-up for Thursday's practical / Greeting: Dear Mr Achebe, / Arrange the body so the request sounds polite, not like an order.
options: I hope you are well.

Many thanks,
Dr Ruth Lang
Would it be possible for you to set them up by 8:45?
We have a class of thirty starting at 9 am on Thursday, and the microscopes need to be ready before then.
quests.hint: A polite request usually gives the reason first and asks last. What sounds least demanding?
quests.explanation: 'Would it be possible' invites a yes or a no. Placing the reason before the request means the technician understands the need before he hears the ask.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You would like a neighbour to move their car from your driveway. Subject: Car in the driveway / Greeting: Dear Mr Sandhu, / Arrange the message.
options:
Thank you for understanding,
Jelena Kovac
I hope you don't mind me writing.
Would you mind parking it in front of your own house from now on?
Your car has been parked across our driveway twice this week, and it made it hard for us to leave for work.
quests.hint: Handle a small conflict by softening first, giving the fact, and then asking politely.
quests.explanation: Starting with 'I hope you don't mind' shows you want to avoid conflict. The fact is stated without accusation, and the request is phrased as a question.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are asking a professor for a deadline extension for the second time. Arrange the email.
options: Dear Professor Yang,
I am very grateful for the extension you gave me last week. Unfortunately, my illness has continued, and I wonder whether I might have until Friday.

Yours sincerely,
Felix Mbeki
Subject: Request for a further extension, Statistics assignment
quests.hint: Because you're asking again, gratitude and honesty should come before the new request.
quests.explanation: Recognising what the professor already did shows respect. 'I wonder whether I might' is the most tentative and polite way to ask, which suits a second request.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A colleague covered your meeting when you were ill. Subject: Thank you for covering / Greeting: Hi Yara, / Arrange the body.
options:
Cheers,
Hector
I heard the client was happy with the presentation, and I really appreciate you taking care of it.
Thank you so much for stepping in on Tuesday.
Let me know if you ever need me to return the favour.
quests.hint: Gratitude, result, offer: what order makes the thanks feel complete?
quests.explanation: Thanks feel stronger when they mention a result. Offering to return the favour shows that you recognise the effort involved.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to thank a customer for a detailed review of your bakery. Put together the email.
options: Subject: Thank you for your kind review

Warm wishes,
The Millers, Corner Loaf Bakery
Dear Ms Wu,
Thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed review of our sourdough. Comments like yours mean a great deal to a small bakery, and we hope to see you again soon.
quests.hint: Thank the person, say what it means, then invite them back.
quests.explanation: Business thanks work best when they name what was appreciated and what it means. The closing invitation encourages the relationship without being pushy.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You wish to thank an interviewer who has taken the time to explain the role by email. Subject: Thank you for the information / Greeting: Dear Ms Ojo, / Arrange the body.
options: Your explanation of the team structure was very helpful.

Yours sincerely,
Adil Rahman
Thank you for your detailed reply to my questions about the role.
I appreciate the time you have given me.
quests.hint: This is a short thank-you, so don't over-elaborate. Which order moves from action to value to courtesy?
quests.explanation: A professional thank-you can be brief: name the action, say what was helpful, then acknowledge their time. It avoids flattery.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have double-booked a customer's table. Arrange the apology to her.
options:
Yours sincerely,
Rafael Duarte, Manager
Subject: Our apology for Saturday's booking
Dear Mrs Aziz,
I am sincerely sorry that we double-booked your table on Saturday, and that you had to wait for forty minutes. This was our mistake, and we would like to invite you back for a complimentary dessert.
quests.hint: A responsible apology names the mistake and does not blame someone else.
quests.explanation: 'This was our mistake' takes clear responsibility. Excuses like 'the system failed' would sound defensive. A remedy shows that you value the customer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You forgot a friend's birthday. Subject: I'm so sorry! / Greeting: Hi Paloma, / Arrange the body.
options: I'm so sorry I forgot your birthday yesterday.
Can I take you out for dinner on Friday to make up for it?
There's no good excuse, and I feel awful about it.

With love,
Theo
quests.hint: In a personal apology, sincerity matters more than length.
quests.explanation: 'There's no good excuse' avoids the trap of explaining. The invitation offers a real way to repair the friendship.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A manager apologises to a team for a confusing message she sent earlier. Subject: Clarification and apology / Greeting: Dear team, / Arrange the body.
options: I should have checked before sending it, and I will be more careful.
The correct deadline for the report is Friday, 20 June, not Thursday.
I want to apologise for my message on Monday, which was unclear about the deadline.

Best regards,
Olga
quests.hint: Apology first, then the correct information, then responsibility for the future.
quests.explanation: In a workplace error, correct information is as important as the apology. Putting it in the middle ensures the team does not miss it, while the last sentence shows accountability.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have to decline a supplier's invitation to a product demonstration. Structure the email.
options: Thank you for inviting me to your demonstration on 5 June. Unfortunately I am unable to attend, but I would be glad to see the materials afterwards.
Dear Mr Novotny,

Kind regards,
Evelyn Shaw
Subject: Re: Invitation to the product demonstration
quests.hint: Decline in a way that keeps the relationship useful.
quests.explanation: A polite refusal of an invitation thanks the sender, gives a clear no, and offers something else. Offering to see the materials keeps the business relationship alive.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A friend asks you to help them move flats, but you have a wedding. Subject: Re: Moving day / Greeting: Hi Gabriel, / Arrange the body.
options: I could come on the Sunday morning to help unpack, if that would be useful.
I'm really sorry, but I can't help on the 21st.

Take care,
Lola
I'm at my sister's wedding all day and won't be free.
quests.hint: Give the refusal early, then the reason, then a small alternative.
quests.explanation: Among friends, direct refusals are appreciated. The alternative of helping on Sunday shows you want to be supportive.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You're turning down a colleague's request to review a long document before a deadline. Subject: Re: Review of the policy draft / Greeting: Hi Martha, / Arrange the body.
options: I'm afraid I don't have the capacity before Friday, because I'm finishing two other reports.
If the deadline could move to Tuesday, I would be happy to help.
Thank you for asking me to review the policy draft.

Best,
Sergio
quests.hint: Decline because of capacity, not because of the person.
quests.explanation: Explaining that you lack capacity keeps the refusal impersonal. Offering a conditional yes gives the colleague a real option.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are giving positive feedback to a team member. Subject: Great work on the client report / Greeting: Hi Tariq, / Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for the extra effort you put in this week.
I wanted to say well done on the client report.
The summary at the start made the main findings clear at a glance, and the client mentioned it in their reply.

Best wishes,
Joanna
quests.hint: Specific praise names what was good and why.
quests.explanation: 'Well done' by itself is forgettable. Naming the summary and the client's reaction helps the person repeat what worked.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You'd like to compliment a chef and ask about a dish. Lay out the email.
options: We had dinner at your restaurant last Friday, and the slow-cooked lamb was the best dish I have eaten this year. Would you be willing to tell me which spices you use?

Kind regards,
Greta Lindqvist
Subject: Compliments and a question about the lamb
Dear Chef Ismail,
quests.hint: A compliment before a request feels natural if it is genuine and specific.
quests.explanation: The compliment explains why you're writing, and the question follows. If the request came first, the compliment would feel like flattery to win a favour.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student writes to a lecturer to say how much she enjoyed the course. Subject: Thank you for the course / Greeting: Dear Professor Ndlovu, / Arrange the body.
options:
Best wishes,
Mariam Sesay
The session on the spice routes changed the way I think about globalisation.
I have decided to write my dissertation on the subject.
I wanted to thank you for your course on the history of trade.
quests.hint: Praise that includes an outcome is the most rewarding for a teacher.
quests.explanation: The final sentence shows the effect on the student's choices. Lecturers rarely hear this, so it makes the message memorable.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A colleague has mentioned that he is short of time. Offer to help. Subject: Offer of help with the mailing / Greeting: Hi Ade, / Arrange the body.
options:
Cheers,
Millie
I heard you're busy with the conference mailing this week.
No worries if you have it under control.
I have some time on Wednesday afternoon if you'd like me to take the second batch.
quests.hint: An offer should be specific, but allow the person to decline.
quests.explanation: Suggesting a definite time makes the offer real. 'No worries if you have it under control' respects the colleague's independence.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A neighbour has broken her leg. Offer support. Subject: Anything I can do? / Greeting: Dear Mrs Pillai, / Arrange the body.
options: I go to the supermarket on Saturdays, so I could pick up your shopping.

Warm wishes,
Callum
Please just text me a list, and I will leave it at your door.
I was very sorry to hear about your leg.
quests.hint: Sympathy, a practical offer, and how to accept it.
quests.explanation: Vague offers such as 'let me know if I can help' are rarely accepted. A specific suggestion and an easy way to respond make a real difference.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You'd like to offer a new colleague some guidance in their first month. Subject: Happy to help / Greeting: Hello Nicolas, / Arrange the body.
options: If you have any questions about systems or processes in your first weeks, please don't hesitate to ask me.
Welcome again to the team.
I usually have lunch at 12:30, so you are welcome to join me.

Kind regards,
Phoebe
quests.hint: The tone is welcoming, so put the offer before the social invitation.
quests.explanation: The professional offer comes first because it is the purpose of the email. The lunch invitation adds warmth without pressure.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You disagree with a colleague's plan to launch in May. Subject: Thoughts on the launch date / Greeting: Hi Winston, / Arrange the body.
options: I agree that we need to move quickly, but I'm concerned that testing won't be complete by May.

Best,
Parisa
Thanks for sharing the launch plan.
Would it be worth moving the launch to June, or could we release a smaller version first?
quests.hint: Agree where you can, state the concern, then suggest alternatives.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging common ground prevents the disagreement from feeling personal. Presenting alternatives makes it a problem-solving conversation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student disagrees with a marker's comment on an essay. Subject: Query about feedback on my essay / Greeting: Dear Dr Kaplan, / Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for the detailed comments on my essay.
I included three sources in the second section, and I wonder whether these might have been overlooked.

Yours sincerely,
Isaac Moyo
I would like to ask about the comment that my argument lacked evidence.
quests.hint: A polite challenge is framed as a question, not as an accusation.
quests.explanation: Saying 'I wonder whether these might have been overlooked' offers a possible explanation without accusing the marker of a mistake.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You wish to disagree with a friend about which restaurant to book. Subject: Re: Restaurant for Saturday / Greeting: Hi Renata, / Arrange the body.
options: I'm a bit worried about the price, though, since Tom is on a tight budget.
How about that Thai place near the station? It's cheaper and has good vegetarian options.

Let me know!
Zoe
I know you love Bella Vita, and it was great last time.
quests.hint: In casual disagreement, give a reason and a suggestion.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging the friend's preference first makes the disagreement gentler. The suggestion shifts the conversation toward a solution.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A colleague you've worked with for years asks you for a favour. Reply in a natural workplace tone. Subject: Re: Can you cover Friday? / Greeting: Hi Jess, / Arrange the body.
options:
Thanks,
Patrick
Just send me the notes when you have a moment.
Yes, no problem, I can cover Friday.
I'll be in from 9 anyway, so it won't be a bother.
quests.hint: Notice how plain and warm this is. Very formal phrases would sound odd between long-time colleagues.
quests.explanation: Over-formality can create distance. When you know someone well, a direct reply is more natural, and it is still polite.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are messaging your yoga instructor, whom you like and see weekly. Subject: Can't make tonight / Greeting: Hi Suki, / Arrange the body.
options: Sorry, I can't make class tonight.

See you then,
Anna
I'll be back next Tuesday!
I've got a work deadline that's run late.
quests.hint: A friendly relationship doesn't need long apologies.
quests.explanation: Your message is short because the relationship is casual. Stating what happened, why, and when you'll return is enough.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: An applicant writes to a start-up whose website is very informal. Subject: Interested in the design role / Greeting: Hi there, / Arrange the body.
options: I'm a designer with three years' experience and would like to find out if you're hiring.
I love the way you use illustration in your app.

Best,
Joel Eriksen
My portfolio is at the link below.
quests.hint: Adapt to the company culture, but stay professional.
quests.explanation: Start-ups often use a more relaxed tone, and matching it shows you understand the culture. Even so, the email remains structured and professional.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are emailing a German professor whose title is 'Professor Dr Keller'. Build the email.
options: I am a Master's student in Chemistry at the University of Lagos and would like to ask whether you are currently accepting doctoral candidates. I have attached my CV for your information.

Yours sincerely,
Chinedu Okafor
Dear Professor Keller,
Subject: Enquiry about your doctoral programme
quests.hint: When titles matter in a culture, use the title of the highest rank you know.
quests.explanation: In many countries, academic titles are important. If in doubt, use 'Professor' rather than 'Mr' or 'Dr', because it is safer than a title that is too low.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are writing to an older neighbour in your building, and you want to be respectful. Subject: Noise from the lift works / Greeting: Dear Mr Abdullah, / Arrange the body.
options:
With kind regards,
Haruka Sato
The building manager has told me that the lift will be out of service on Monday and Tuesday.
I hope you are keeping well.
If you need help with shopping or other errands on those days, please do let me know.
quests.hint: Respect can be shown by asking about wellbeing and offering help.
quests.explanation: Traditional courtesy, such as asking after someone's health, shows respect. The offer of help is particularly appreciated by elderly neighbours.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are writing to a hotel abroad and are unsure how to greet the manager. Arrange the email.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Monique Laurent
Subject: Booking enquiry for July
We would like to book a double room from 12 to 19 July. Could you please confirm availability and send the rates?
Dear Sir or Madam,
quests.hint: When you don't know the person or the customs, choose the most neutral formal greeting.
quests.explanation: 'Dear Sir or Madam' is safe when you do not know the recipient. Most hotels understand and reply politely, and you avoid assumptions about gender or titles.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are replying to a customer who has complained politely. Lay out the email; pay attention to tone.
options: Subject: Re: Your comments about order 40817
Dear Mr Pereira,

Yours sincerely,
Chloe Barton
Thank you for letting us know about the scratch on your table. I am sorry it arrived damaged, and I have arranged for a replacement to be delivered on Thursday.
quests.hint: Thank, apologise, solve. Notice how the customer's politeness is matched.
quests.explanation: A courteous complaint deserves an equally courteous reply. Thanking the customer first shows that feedback is welcome, and the concrete solution completes the apology.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are a student asking a busy professor for a short meeting. Piece together the email.
options: Dear Professor Grant,
Subject: Request for a short meeting about my dissertation
I am writing to ask whether you might have twenty minutes in the next two weeks to discuss my dissertation proposal. I am happy to work around your timetable.

Yours sincerely,
Hana Kobayashi
quests.hint: Tentative phrasing and flexibility show respect for a busy person.
quests.explanation: 'Whether you might have' and 'happy to work around your timetable' show that you value the professor's time, which makes a yes more likely.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You're sending a friendly reminder to a friend who owes you a small amount of money. Set out the message.
options: Hope you're doing well! Just a quick reminder about the £15 for the concert tickets, whenever you get a chance.
Hi Ollie,
Subject: Quick reminder

Thanks!
Mina
quests.hint: Money reminders between friends should be light and low-pressure.
quests.explanation: A warm opening and 'whenever you get a chance' keep the tone friendly. The exact amount and reason prevent confusion without awkwardness.
